To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the calcium-deficient form (CDNA) of influenza virus neuramidase (NA): 1) contains a calcium-binding site that is not occupied by calcium in CDNA, 2) contains an additional calcium-binding site that may not be occupied by calcium in the wild-type enzyme, and 3) has an active-site sulfate ion that is not found in the wild-type NA.
calcium is required for substrate binding in influenza virus neuraminide, and that the structure of the enzyme is altered in the absence of calcium.

the X-ray structure of an influenza virus neuraminindase isolated from whale has been determined and that the structure of this enzyme is altered by the absence of calcium ions that are usually found in this protein, resulting in changes in substrate binding.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of substrate binding and catalysis by influenza virus neuraminidease (NA), the enzyme responsible for the release of newly formed viral particles from the host cell.
understanding the molecular basis of influenza virus replication, the development of antiviral compounds and the development of a vaccine against influenza virus infection.
the molecular basis of substrate and inhibitor recognition by influenza virus NA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the X-ray crystallographic studies of influenza virus neuramidase (NA), which are described in this thesis, have provided a wealth of information on the structure and mechanism of action of this important enzyme, which is the target of a number of antiviral drugs.
this is the first time that the calcium-deficient form has been observed in the X-ray structure determination of a protein.

the structure of the calcium-deficient form, in which calcium is absent, is a new structure that has been observed for the first time in the influenza virus NA and that the calcium-free structure is the active structure of the enzyme.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the structure of influenza virus NA has been refined at 2.1 A and that the structure has been solved for an enzyme in which the calcium ion is absent.
this study provides a structural basis for understanding substrate binding to NA and for the rational design of inhibitors of the enzyme.
the calcium-deficient NA structure is the first example of a calcium-free neuraminidase and provides a new model for substrate and inhibitor design.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is important to consider the possibility of calcium deficiency when interpreting X-ray structures of proteins and when designing inhibitors of enzymes that contain a bound calcium ion.
it is not the calcium that is important for substrate binding but rather its absence.
the absence of calcium in the substrate-binding site results in conformational changes that are important for substrate binding.
